growing_specifications.description: High-demand rapid-cycling vining fruit vegetable cultivated on vertical bamboo trellises across Philippine lowlands. Famous for its crisp, cylindrical, refreshing fruits with over 95% water content and high yield potential.

category_why.title: Why is Cucumber classified under Cucurbit / Climbing Vine?
category_why.summary: Cucumis sativus belongs to the gourd family (Cucurbitaceae), growing as an indeterminate climbing herbaceous vine with coiled tendrils and monoecious yellow flowers.
points: Climbing Vine Morphology: Produces slender vines that climb 2–3 meters along vertical trellis netting, elevating fruit off the ground to prevent contact decay.
High Water Pepo Fruit: Yields cylindrical green fruits with crisp, watery flesh containing 95% moisture and mild flavor.
Rapid Turnover: One of the fastest-producing cucurbits, beginning harvest in 35–45 days and continuing for several weeks.

harvest_why.title: Why is harvest maturity set to 35–50 days with daily/alternate-day picking?
harvest_why.summary: Fast cell enlargement requires frequent harvesting (every 1–2 days) to capture crisp, tender, dark green fruits before they turn pale, yellow, or seed-hardened.
points: Emergence & Seedling Phase (Days 1–10): True seeds germinate in 4–7 days with rapid true leaf expansion.
Vegetative & Trellis Training (Days 10–25): Fast vine elongation, lateral shoot pruning, and trellis climbing.
Flowering to First Harvest (Days 25–40): Yellow blossoms develop into market-ready fruits within 10–14 days after pollination.
Continuous 1–2 Day Picking Frequency: Harvesting every 1–2 days stimulates continuous flower bud setting and prevents fruit from turning yellow and bitter.

watering_why.title: Why does Cucumber require consistent watering every 2 days?
watering_why.summary: With 95% fruit water content and shallow fibrous root systems, inconsistent moisture triggers cucurbitacin bitterness and curved, deformed fruits.
points: Cucurbitacin Bitterness Suppression: Moisture deficits trigger natural defensive cucurbitacins in the rind and stem end, making cucumbers astringent and bitter.
Crooked Fruit Prevention: Steady transpiration ensures uniform bilateral cell division, producing straight, cylindrical, premium-grade fruits.
Root Aeration: Proper furrow/drip irrigation prevents stagnant waterlogging and root rot while keeping moisture at 60–70% field capacity.

soil_why.title: Why does Cucumber thrive in well-drained loam (pH 5.5–6.8) on raised beds?
soil_why.summary: Friable, organic-rich soil ensures fast root penetration while raised beds protect against root suffocation and soil-borne damping-off.
points: Raised Bed Aeration: 20 cm elevated beds safeguard root systems from waterlogging during heavy tropical downpours.
Nutrient Availability: A pH of 5.5–6.8 optimizes uptake of Potassium (80–120 kg/ha) for fruit bulking and Calcium to prevent blossom-end distortion.
Organic Matter: Compost incorporation retains essential moisture and supports beneficial soil microbial activity.

varieties.description: Leading commercial slicing hybrid in the Philippines from East-West Seed. Produces uniform, straight, dark green cylindrical fruits (18–22 cm) with thick, crispy flesh and strong tolerance to Downy Mildew and CMV.
Crisp green hybrid cucumber with dark rind, high moisture content, and outstanding field resistance to powdery mildew and fruit rot.
High-vigor hybrid bred for heavy continuous fruiting, sweet crisp flesh, and excellent shelf life for commercial wholesale markets.
Traditional open-pollinated native slicing cucumber adapted to backyard gardens, producing tender, juicy fruits with refreshing flavor.
